newsitem.title: USA: U.S. presidential race tightens in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presidential race tightens in Reuters poll.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole closed the gap with President Bill Clinton to about 9 percentage points in the latest Reuters daily tracking poll on Monday, a leap from 15 points behind in the previous survey.

The poll -- completed before the first presidential debate on Sunday night in Hartford, Connecticut -- was conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International and had Clinton at 44.4 percent, Dole, 35.1 percent and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, 5.8 percent.

This poll was a rolling three day average of polling results from Friday through Sunday. The Reuters/Zogby poll of approximately 900 likely voters had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percentage points.
"I'm calling this the October adjustment we've all been expecting," pollster John Zogby said, noting there was no single event that caused the race to tighten.
Dole is solidifying his Republican base and "is now getting three out of four Republican voters," Zogby said.
Earlier Dole could count on only about 62 to 64 percent of Republicans surveyed, Zogby said.
"One could anticipate there will be a little more tightening as he brings in more Republicans," Zogby said.
Dole's move from 15 percentage points behind in the poll released on Sunday to nine points was a big jump, but Zogby described the recent polling this way:

"We've had a wild ride over the past few days. First Clinton received a big bounce from the Middle East summit and at its peak had a 20-point lead over Dole. But over the weekend, the gap has narrowed to single digits in single day results and factored together, (it) produces this incredible turnaround."

The poll showed the race for the House of Representatives was neck and neck with 37.9 percent of voters saying they will Democrat while 35.6 percent said they will vote Republican on Nov. 5. In the contest for the Senate, voters say they prefer Republicans 41.4 percent to 37.4 percent.
